newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks French to let truckers pass.
newsitem.headline: EU asks French to let truckers pass.

text.p: The European Commission asked French authorities and unions on Friday to act urgently to allow trucks from other European Union countries to use roads blockaded by striking truck drivers.

"The roadblocks are producing extremely serious consequences for the free circulation of people and goods from other member states, which is one of the fundamental rights of the Union," Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti said in a statement.
Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said he had written to trade union leaders asking them to allow non-French truck drivers to return home before the weekend.

"The drivers affected by the dispute are in a very difficult situation, in some cases having now spent more than 11 days in the blockades and many of them are without food, money or warm conditions," he said in a separate statement.

The 12-day-old strike has stranded up to 14,000 Spanish trucks and idled about 90 percent of Portugal's total truck fleet. Belgian ports are clogged by lorries forced to detour from the French Channel port of Calais.

The strikers have already relaxed the Calais blockade to let stranded British trucks get on ferries for home. Kinnock said union officials had also told him that non-French truckers were being allowed to drive to Italy.
Kinnock told the unions that the Commission was considering possible improvements to EU legislation "that would directly address some of the root causes of discontent in the (trucking) sector".
He noted that it was drafting a paper that would look at the possibility of extending EU rules on working hours and rest periods to truck drivers.

EU ministers were also debating whether to adopt legislation that would introduce a new generation of electronic "tachographs" into cabs to monitor whether drivers stick to limits on daily driving time, he said.
Strikers met employers on Friday to sign deals on some of their demands, which involve retirement age, pay, working hours and rest periods.
